question: Can a campaign start transmitting new election ads to the public in a federal riding on polling day while polls are still open there?
generated_answer:
In Canada, the Canada Elections Act prohibits the transmission of election advertising on polling day, while the polls are open. This is known as the "blackout period".

According to Section 323 of the Canada Elections Act, no person shall transmit election advertising to the public on polling day, from the opening of the polls until the closing of the polls, in an electoral district where the election is being held.

This means that a campaign cannot start transmitting new election ads to the public in a federal riding on polling day while polls are still open there. Any election advertising that was already running before polling day can continue to run, but no new ads can be transmitted during the blackout period.

It's worth noting that this prohibition applies to all forms of election advertising, including television, radio, print, and online ads. The goal of the blackout period is to prevent campaigns from influencing voters on their way to the polls or while they are waiting in line to vote.
